metaTitle: Color Profiles Explained: ICC, sRGB, and Color Management
metaDescription: Learn what color profiles are, why they matter, and how to avoid mismatched colors when preparing images for web and print.

guideContent.section1Title: Why color profiles are part of a professional workflow
guideContent.section1Body: Color profiles help define how colors should be interpreted across devices and software. Without them, the same image can look slightly different on a phone, monitor, printer, or design app. That difference matters when the image needs to look precise and consistent.
guideContent.section2Title: How to avoid common color mistakes
guideContent.section2Body: A practical workflow uses a profile that matches the output destination, especially for brand assets and print work. Web projects often lean toward sRGB, while print workflows may require a wider or more specific profile.
steps: Identify whether the asset is for screen, print, or a brand system.
Use a profile that matches the destination, especially for logo and brand work.
Test the file on the device or printer that will receive it.

faqs.question: What is an ICC profile?
faqs.answer: It is a color profile that helps software interpret and reproduce colors consistently across devices.

faqs.question: Why do colors look different on different screens?
faqs.answer: Because devices vary in hardware, calibration, and color space interpretation.

faqs.question: Should I always convert to sRGB for web?
faqs.answer: For many web workflows, yes, because it is the most widely supported color space.
